browser_chrome_identity_surface_label: Example browser-chrome identity posture for official voter-information routes
delivery_role_note: Bounded page-title and browser-chrome identity surface for official voter-information routes that voters may revisit through tabs, history entries, or app-switcher labels.
page_title_pattern_note: Page titles name the task or answer first and keep office/site branding at the end so tabs and history entries remain route-legible.
task_first_labeling_note: Materially different states such as entry, result, review, and confirmation use distinct task-first title labels.
office_and_jurisdiction_context_note: Titles preserve enough office or jurisdiction context to distinguish state, county, or municipal election routes that would otherwise share the same task label.
client_side_title_update_note: Single-page navigation updates the document title whenever the effective official route or route state changes.
title_heading_breadcrumb_alignment_note: Page title, visible heading, and breadcrumb wording tell the same truth about the route topic and state even if they are not character-for-character identical.
sensitive_title_data_minimization_note: Titles distinguish route states without exposing long personal identifiers, full secret tokens, or unnecessary personal details in browser chrome.
must_distinguish_states: entry step vs review step vs confirmation step
history_entry_disambiguation_note: Routes that differ in task or authoritative next step remain distinguishable in tabs and history entries instead of collapsing into one generic portal title.
